source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Aminoglycosides can impair neuromuscular transmission and may intensify weakness or produce neuromuscular blockade in susceptible clients.","B":"Aminoglycosides increase acetylcholine release and are first-line treatment for the underlying autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disorder.","C":"Gentamicin has no clinically relevant effect on neuromuscular function, so myasthenia gravis does not influence risk assessment.","D":"The principal concern is predictable severe hypertension from aminoglycoside therapy rather than worsening neuromuscular weakness or blockade."}}
source_row.rationale: Gentamicin and other aminoglycosides can impair neuromuscular transmission and worsen weakness or neuromuscular blockade in myasthenia gravis, so the order requires careful risk review.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings/precautions: aminoglycosides have neuromuscular-blocking properties and should be used cautiously in disorders characterized by muscular weakness such as myasthenia gravis. Current DailyMed gentamicin injection labeling rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Why is an aminoglycoside such as gentamicin concerning in a client with myasthenia gravis?
